## The short version

I am a public policy researcher from Guntur, in coastal Andhra Pradesh. I read Political Science at Acharya Nagarjuna University for both my degrees, finishing the master's as the highest-ranked graduate in my cohort, and I am joining University College London in September 2026 for an MSc in Public Policy as a Commonwealth Scholar.

My research sits at the point where a policy stops being a document and starts being an encounter — a farmer at a bank counter, a village resident at a block office, a teacher in a school that a budget line forgot. I am interested in what the state's own measurements do and do not see at that point.

## What I work on

<ul class="interests">
<li>State capacity and public administration</li>
<li>Citizen–state relations and the co-production of public services</li>
<li>Welfare delivery, targeting, and programme evaluation</li>
<li>Street-level implementation and bureaucratic performance</li>
<li>Participatory governance and citizen monitoring</li>
</ul>

## Methods

**Qualitative and field-based.** Village-level fieldwork, community engagement, interviews, comparative policy analysis, legislative research, policy brief writing, and grant proposal development including methodology design and budgeting.

**Quantitative.** Working knowledge of R, Stata and SPSS, alongside Excel and Power BI, applied to migration data analysis, comparative budget analysis and welfare delivery tracking. I am building on this ahead of methods training at UCL.

**Fieldwork languages.** Telugu is my first language and I am fluent in Hindi, which lets me run interviews and translation for India-based qualitative work without an intermediary.

## Beyond research

I mentor first-generation students towards higher education as a volunteer with the Eklavya India Foundation. As a student leader in 2022 I helped secure scholarships for more than a thousand students from marginalised backgrounds through collective advocacy with university and state authorities, and between 2021 and 2023 I led outreach at the Mother Teresa Foundation supporting orphaned and elderly people.
